song.title: You’re The Best Mum For Me!
song.author: Mark and Helen Johnson
song.summary: What better way to show our appreciation to mums everywhere, than with a song of gratitude and celebration. A simple song with a simple message: ‘You’re the best mum for me!’
song.teachingTips:
• There are lots of words in this song that all need to be sung clearly, so start with a warm-up that focuses on diction such as Peter Piper from S!ng Warm-Ups.
  • There is lots of nice easy stepwise movement in this melody, but the occasional semitones will need practice, e.g. notice the difference between the notes of the first ‘It’s a good’ in bar 4 and the ‘it’s a good’ in bar 8.
  • Help the children to know when to come in at the end of the first time bar. Listen out for two upbeats in the brass and then come in with ‘It’s a’ on the third one.

assembly.title: People Who Care
assembly.description: The ideal assembly to help us to focus on, appreciate and celebrate all those who help and care for us.

resources.title: Exploring Rests
resources.content:
[{"key":"4f665ce47ef9ba67","layout":"icon-bullet","attributes":{"body":"
  • To keep a steady pulse
  • To explore rests in music
  • To listen to a rhythm and clap it back (call and response)
  • To begin to sing confidently and in time. 
","title":"What’s achievable","image":"https://assets.sparkyard.com/uploads/icons/green-star-1614702483w2iKm.png"}},{"key":"44deddf2fdca95fa","layout":"icon-bullet","attributes":{"body":"

Amplified sound system; backing track for this song 

","title":"What you need","image":"https://assets.sparkyard.com/uploads/icons/blue-wrench-16147025258WedI.png"}},{"key":"db69cf2f17d54387","layout":"wysiwyg","attributes":{"body":"

First, listen to the song and feel its strong four-beat pulse by clapping or tapping along, saying 1 2 3 4 1 2 3 4 with emphasis on the 1 each time (perhaps add a stamp on this beat).

Now, listen carefully to the melody line. Explain that a rest is a period of silence in a piece of music (not a time for lying down!). Can the class identify where there are rests in the music? To demonstrate this, say ‘sh’ with a finger to the lips in each of the rests. Sometimes there will be one ‘sh’ (a one-beat rest e.g. after ‘I love you Mum’ and ‘you’re the best’) and sometimes two (a two-beat rest e.g. after ‘best mum for me!’).

Sitting or standing in a circle, have half the class keeping the pulse steady by tapping their knees. Clap some four-beat rhythms with rests in, for the other half of the class to copy. Then swap over groups. For example: 

","title":"","background_color":""}},{"key":"693ca4af8a5ac3b6","layout":"image","attributes":{"image":"https://assets.sparkyard.com/uploads/MusicActivities/musicactivities-exploring-rests-16165860382BLKC.png","title":"","background_color":""}},{"key":"b835fef57196a780","layout":"wysiwyg","attributes":{"body":"

With older or more confident pupils, each could clap their response individually. Can the children say which beat of the bar the rest was on? Would one pupil like to lead by clapping a ‘rest rhythm’ for the others to copy? 

","title":"","background_color":""}},{"key":"1a70e02f674602f7","layout":"video","attributes":{"url":"https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sb-2VsE2y-U","title":"The Percussion Show - Body Percussion ","background_color":""}},{"key":"9bbf8016d861b13c","layout":"icon-bullet","attributes":{"body":"

In a circle, tapping the pulse on the knees, all sing ‘It’s a good time to tell you, I love you Mum’. Now replace ‘you Mum’ with other words suggested by the children such as ‘baked beans’, ‘football’, ‘my dog’ etc. They’ll need to think of two-syllable phrases. Do a few together to get the idea. Then go around the circle and point to a volunteer (sitting with their hand raised) who would like to sing their suggestion while everyone else keeps the pulse going. This game encourages confidence and singing in time. 

","title":"Branch Out","image":"https://assets.sparkyard.com/uploads/icons/u1874-1614695090s5QJx.png"}}]
resources.summary: Explore rests in music and have fun with some call-and-response rhythms.

resources.title: ‘I Love You, Mum!’ Flowerpots
resources.content:
[{"key":"694d1bacd142a1d5","layout":"wysiwyg","attributes":{"body":"

Make some beautiful ‘I love you, Mum!’ flowerpots. Cut out a flowerpot shape from coloured card for each child and ask them to write ‘I love you, Mum!’ on them. On a different coloured piece of card ask each child to draw round their hand. Cut these out and stick the bottom of the hand to the top of the flowerpot shape. Next, cut out lots of different coloured flower shapes and give five to each child. Ask them to write something on each that describes their Mum, e.g. ‘kind’, ‘patient’, ‘lovely smile’, ‘best hugs’, ‘good at stories’ and stick a flower on top of each finger!<\/p>\n","title":"","noMargin":false}}]
